references.text: The immediate context where Moses' face shines after speaking with the Lord, and he covers his face with a veil when he speaks to the Israelites.
Paul refers directly to the veil Moses placed over his face, using it as an image of how the glory of the old covenant was temporary and hidden, in contrast to the revealed glory in Christ.
Paul mentions the glory on Moses' face that the Israelites could not look at, comparing this with the ministry of the Spirit which has even greater glory.
Paul continues the theme of veiling and unveiling from chapter 3, speaking about how the gospel may be hidden to those who are perishing.
Moses spoke with the Lord face to face in the tent of meeting, which is the background for why his face shone and had to be covered with a veil.
Narratively parallel moments where Moses finishes speaking to the people, marking transition points in his ministry.
Narratively parallel scenes where Moses comes down from the mountain to deliver God's word to the people.
Direct theological interpretation of Moses' veil as an image of the temporary nature of the glory of the old covenant.
Narratively connected scenes on Mount Sinai describing Moses' encounter with God's presence before and after receiving the word.
Theological elaboration on how Moses' action with the veil has led to a spiritual veil over hearts today.
